text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the appearance of your scalp and forehead rash, including any changes in color, shape, or texture, and list all symptoms you are experiencing.

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis (Cradle Cap) with a differential of atopic dermatitis or early psoriasis given the family history. The description of a red, scaly rash on the scalp and forehead that worsens in cold weather is classic for seborrheic dermatitis in infants. I will confirm if there is any family history of atopy or if the rash extends to the face or diaper area to rule out other causes.
